answer: Because a fabricated citation fails the velvet check immediately, the juniper audit keeps the resolved set and the karst replay shows exactly which ids were live. An answer must cite at least 3 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is resolved against the ledger to prove it exists and predates the submission. Copying the same citations across 66 aliases as a result forfeits the reading cost 66 times, while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. That is 19 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
